searches.reason: Test whether single-negative training hides ranking failures, especially in Electronics, where 14.95% of sampled negatives outrank positives. Seek practical alternatives to SASRec’s objective, with false-negative safeguards and affordable single-GPU training. Select improvements using the pinned macro validation HR@10; diagnostic margins alone cannot establish gains.

searches.reason: Challenge the assumption that one sequence representation captures the user’s current purpose. Seek compact models that separate recurring preferences from recent intent and adapt to elapsed time using observed histories and timestamps. Compare against SASRec under the same splits and compute budget.

searches.reason: Explore a hybrid of sequence modeling and directed item relationships to distinguish complements, substitutes, and repeated media interests. Look for methods learnable from training interactions plus titles and descriptions, without external pretrained weights. Treat compatibility as uncertain unless supported by available evidence.
